rows.end_mark: Only the end mark, ampersand B at the close of an article, may stand under 16 px, at the text's cap height, because it follows a word and names nothing on its own (DR-130, Rules 03.4 and 04.6). On a 1x screen it is drawn on whole pixels and sits on the baseline: the 14 px end mark master, 13 by 13 px, in 17 px text and the 12 px end mark master, 11 by 11 px, in 15 px text (DR-180). On every other screen and at other text sizes it stands 16/14 of the text's cap height tall, from the 16 px master

rows.status_note: The 48 px master joined on November 8, 2026 (DR-131). Since November 10, 2026 the 24 and 48 px files in use draw each node and the lever as one outline, the same pixels as the earlier files at 24 and 48 px, so their nodes stay whole between those sizes (DR-145, DR-181). The earlier files, one rect per pixel row, stay in lockmark/ for the record (record_files). The 48 px master still serves 48 px only, the size its pixel grid was drawn for: between whole multiples of its grid its edges fall between pixels (work/handoffs/phase-2/20261109_Stage-B-Identity-Notes.md, section 2)
